Event organizers do not sit at a desk waiting for a pitch. They have a theme and an audience problem, so they type that problem into LinkedIn, Google, or ChatGPT, and they book whoever shows up looking like a safe bet. Getting invited to speak is a search problem and a trust problem at the same time.

This video covers the system behind every speaking invite I landed this year with zero outreach: the five author data fields that travel with every post (name, headline, company, industry, title) and how LinkedIn's LLM scores them against an organizer's own profile block, the cold start behavior that makes an organizer's job title do the matching work, the two profile moves almost nobody makes, the hot and warm framework for the featured section, the three post types that put you in front of organizers, and what speaker bureaus really do with a listing. Real proof runs through it: a $5,000 paid keynote in Guangzhou on the 103rd floor, booked off LinkedIn with no email sent.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
 The mental checklist an organizer runs before they message you
 The five author data fields carrying your distribution on every post
 Why cold start means an organizer's job title does the matching
 How to write a headline that pays your business and still gets you booked
 The two searchable profile settings that take under five minutes
 Hot and warm: fitting speaking into a featured section that already has a job
 The three post types that get organizers to your booking page
 When speaking for free is the right yes

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Your profile answers an organizer's questions before you ever get a message, and if it does not, there is no message
 LinkedIn converts your post plus your author data into one block of text and scores it against every member's block for closeness in meaning
 When someone has almost no engagement history, LinkedIn infers their interests from their headline and job title alone, which describes most event organizers
 The services section set to public speaking puts you in a searchable directory event planners filter by service and location
 Listing the actual talk title next to a past event tells an organizer you have a session they can slot into a track
 A DM asking whether you speak means the profile did not close the decision
